why: mixlab -mode prepare preserves input record order. Speech Commands enumerates class by class, so writing records in that order makes every shard nearly single-label. Nothing errors; the run trains at full throughput and produces a model barely above chance.
dataset: Speech Commands v0.02, 84,843 train records, 35 classes, 1,369 shards, ~62 records per shard
model: 6-layer bidirectional S4D classifier, identical config and seed in both arms
finding: Same config, same seed, same code: 3.52 vs 92.50 at epoch 1, a gap of 88.98 accuracy points. The class-ordered arm was still at 4.26 by epoch 18, so this is not a slow start.
fix_in_this_recipe: scripts/prep_sc35.py permutes all three splits with a fixed seed before writing, and permutes labels with the same index array.
related: The in-training `acc=` is a 10-batch sample. Over class-ordered data those batches are one class, so it reads near zero whether or not the model is learning.
provenance: Early diagnostic run during development, on mixlab 0.105.1. Both arms used the same config and seed as each other; that config file was not preserved, so this is evidence for the effect rather than a reproduction procedure. The permutation fix it motivated is in scripts/prep_sc35.py and is exercised by every run here.
